- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- When sentiment swings from high to low, model frequently fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
